name: discover-mode severity gate in isolation
question: Does argus fail a discover run on the severity gate alone, with no broken build involved?
why: Blocked here, and argus CI does not cover it either. tests/dockerfiles/broken/Dockerfile is in every discover run, so any run that could observe the severity gate (allow_failure=false) has already failed on the build gate. Needs a repo with no broken Dockerfile, or a search_paths input on container-scan.yml's discover step. Remote-mode C3-C6 walk the severity ladder instead.

name: finding counts and per-scanner status from a caller
question: Can a caller of container-scan.yml see how many vulnerabilities were found, or which scanner found them?
why: Not observable. container-scan.yml declares no workflow_call outputs, so a consumer only sees the job result. The scanner-container action does expose counts and argus CI asserts on them, so the logic is covered; what is untested is the reusable-workflow contract. E12 works around it by downloading the scan artifact. Asking argus for workflow_call outputs would close this properly.

name: exit code for an unscannable image
question: Does argus exit non-zero when an image cannot be pulled and nothing could be scanned?
why: Deliberately untested because argus states no contract. container-scan.yml does not pass --fail-on-scanner-error and fail_on_severity is none, so whether a total scan failure is fatal is undefined. R9 accepts both outcomes; tighten it once argus decides.

name: private registry authentication success path
question: Does argus successfully pull and scan an image from a private registry using real credentials?
why: Only the failure path is tested. E8 covers registry_username set with the registry_password secret missing. A successful private pull needs real credentials in repository secrets, which this suite deliberately does not hold.

name: GHES runtime behaviour
question: Does argus actually run correctly on GitHub Enterprise Server?
why: Only statically checked. U5 and I2 grep the action scripts for hardcoded github.com URLs. Nothing executes against a real GHES instance, and the composite-action path GHES users are told to take is not exercised end to end.

name: multi-arch and non-amd64 images
question: Does argus scan an arm64 or multi-architecture image correctly from an amd64 runner?
why: Not covered anywhere. Every image in this suite is pulled for the runner's native amd64 architecture. Platform selection, manifest-list handling and emulation are untested.

name: SARIF size limits
question: Does argus handle a SARIF upload that exceeds GitHub's size or result-count limits?
why: Not covered. E11 tests the empty-SARIF end only. GitHub rejects SARIF over 10MB or 25000 results, which a full trivy+grype scan of a very vulnerable image can approach.

name: pull request comment rendering from a consumer
question: Does a consumer of container-scan.yml get a correctly formatted pull request comment?
why: Partly covered upstream. argus CI tests the security-summary action that renders and posts the comment, but no test here runs container-scan.yml in a pull_request context, so the end-to-end path including comment_marker dedup and comment updating is unexercised from a caller's side.

name: top-level security-scan and hardening workflows
question: Does security-scan.yml or reusable-security-hardening.yml work end to end?
why: Genuinely untested, here and upstream. reusable-security-hardening.yml is referenced only by security-reusable-demo.yml, which is workflow_dispatch-only and therefore never runs automatically. No test workflow in argus invokes it, and this suite covers container-scan.yml, infrastructure-scan.yml and container-scan-from-config.yml only. This is the orchestration layer most consumers would actually call.

name: scanner-container and scanner-container-summary actions
question: Do the scanner-container and scanner-container-summary composite actions work?
why: Covered by argus CI: test-actions.yml runs both directly. Out of scope here because container-scan.yml no longer routes through them as of argus 1.x, so they are not on this suite's consumer path.

name: secret scanning (gitleaks)
question: Does argus detect secrets committed to a repository?
why: Covered by argus CI: the test-secrets job in test-actions.yml exercises the scanner-gitleaks action. Out of scope here; this suite tests the container and IaC scanning workflows.

name: Python SAST (bandit) and code scanning (opengrep, codeql)
question: Does argus detect insecure Python code, or run SAST over a repository?
why: Covered by argus CI: the test-bandit, test-opengrep and test-codeql jobs exercise those actions directly, and argus/tests holds their unit tests. Out of scope here.

name: dependency and supply-chain scanning
question: Does argus detect vulnerable dependencies, or verify supply-chain provenance?
why: Covered by argus CI: test-osv, test-supply-chain and test-dependency-review exercise those actions. Out of scope here.

name: DAST web application scanning (ZAP)
question: Does argus scan a running web application for vulnerabilities?
why: Covered by argus CI: test-zap and test-parse-zap-config exercise the ZAP action and its config parser. Out of scope here.

name: linter actions
question: Does argus lint Dockerfiles, Python, YAML, JavaScript, JSON or Terraform?
why: Covered by argus CI: all six linter-* actions plus linting-summary have their own jobs in test-actions.yml. Out of scope here.

name: AI summary action
question: Does argus generate an AI summary of scan results?
why: Covered by argus CI: test-ai-summary.yml exercises the ai-summary action. Out of scope here.

name: setup-argus and security-summary actions
question: Do the setup-argus and security-summary composite actions work?
why: Covered by argus CI: test-setup-argus and test-security-summary exercise them directly. This suite reaches both indirectly, since container-scan.yml installs argus with one and stitches its summary with the other, but does not assert on them.

name: argus CLI and Python package
question: Does the argus command line tool work when invoked directly, outside GitHub Actions?
why: Covered by argus CI: test-unit.yml runs the full pytest suite across argus/tests with an 80% coverage gate, including test_cli.py. Out of scope here; this suite reaches the CLI only through the reusable workflows.

name: container exposure and services scanners
question: Does argus detect exposed ports or running services in a container image?
why: Covered by argus CI: argus/tests/scanners/test_container.py and argus/tests/test_container_scanner.py exercise the exposure and services scan paths. Not reachable from this suite because container-scan.yml defaults to trivy,grype,syft and does not expose those scanner keys.
